0.title: Mindful Breath & Body Check-In
0.description: Take a pause each morning and evening to breathe deeply and scan your body for tension, a technique that builds your awareness of immediate physical and emotional states. Set a timer for 5 minutes and practice noticing how the world sounds, smells, and feels while you breathe.
0.sourceSentence: Wherever you are beginning this, take a deep breath and notice how you feel in your body, and how the world around you feels.

0.title: Tiny Observations: Ants, Lizard, and Rain
0.description: Observe a small natural phenomenon (e.g., ants on a ceiling, a lizard peeking, rain patterns) for a few minutes each day. Record what you see, how it moves, and what patterns emerge. Use this practice to cultivate the skill of spotting emergent patterns in everyday life.
0.sourceSentence: there is a trail of ants moving along the ceiling of my room, and the sounds of a small jungle town ...

6.title: Deep Listening Practice
6.description: Set aside 20 minutes each day to listen to a conversation or observation without forming a response or judgment, engaging all senses to fully absorb the experience.
6.sourceSentence: I am listening now with all of my senses

6.title: Pattern Mapping
6.description: Keep a daily journal noting recurring themes or subtle messages in your interactions, then every week summarize the patterns you detect and explore their significance.
6.sourceSentence: I notice that the more I pay attention, the more I see order, clear messages, patterns, and invitations in the small or seemingly random things that happen in my life.

6.title: Humility in Action
6.description: Identify one person you consider an authority or knowing figure and ask them for a lesson or perspective. Record what you learn and reflect on how relinquishing resistance opened this space.
6.sourceSentence: It’s been hard and rewarding work to relinquish some of that resistance in order to let wisdom in.

6.title: Love-Driven Collaboration
6.description: Initiate a small collaborative project within your community where decisions are guided by love, inclusivity, and shared well‑being rather than competition or domination.
6.sourceSentence: If love were the central practice of a new generation of organizers and spiritual leaders, it would have a massive impact on what was considered organizing.

10.title: Future Imagination Exercise
10.description: Set aside 30 minutes each week to brainstorm possible futures for a specific social issue using mind maps, creative prompts, or rapid sketching. Document each scenario and reflect on its feasibility.

10.title: Collaborative Ideation Workshop
10.description: Organize a structured ideation session with a diverse group to design a future economy or ecology that centers people and the planet. Use techniques like affinity mapping, role-playing, and rapid prototyping to generate shared concepts.
10.sourceSentence: We must imagine new worlds that transition ideologies and norms, so that no one sees Black people as murderers, or Brown people as terrorists and aliens, but all of us as potential cultural and economic innovators.

10.title: Reframe Racial Imaginations
10.description: Write a personal reflection on how racialized fears shape your perceptions. Then craft an inclusive narrative or visual piece counteracting those narratives and share it with a community or online platform to spark dialogue.
10.sourceSentence: And that imagination is so respected that those who kill, based on an imagined, racialized fear of Black people, are rarely held accountable.

10.title: Science Fiction Story Sprint
10.description: Write a short science‑fiction vignette depicting a world where justice and ecological balance reign supreme. Use the story as a case study to extract actionable principles for real‑world change.
10.sourceSentence: Science fiction is simply a way to practice the future together.

13.title: Learn Biomimicry Principles for Movement Design
13.description: Study biomimicry models, identify natural systems that align with your movement’s goals, and design organizational structures that emulate those resilient patterns.
13.sourceSentence: Biomimitics or biomimicry is the imitation of the models, systems, and elements of nature for the purpose of solving complex human problems.

13.title: Apply Permaculture Concepts to Community Practices
13.description: Analyze permaculture principles such as ecosystem simulation, and apply them to your community’s social and agricultural actions to create sustainable, resilient patterns.
13.sourceSentence: Permaculture is a system of agricultural and social design principles centered around simulating or directly utilizing the patterns and features observed in natural ecosystems.

13.title: Facilitate Simple Interaction Workshops
13.description: Design and run workshops that teach participants how to use intentional, simple interactions to spark complex system changes, emphasizing adaptability, decentralization, and collective awareness.
13.sourceSentence: Leverage relatively simple interactions to create complex patterns, systems, and transformations—including adaptation, interdependence and decentralization, fractal awareness, resilience and transformative justice, nonlinear and iterative change.

13.title: Practice Relational Leadership in Your Team
13.description: Build and practice relational leadership techniques inspired by Octavia Butler’s model, focusing on mutual recognition, shared decision‑making, and continuous feedback loops.
13.sourceSentence: A relational leadership model found in the work of Black science fiction writer Octavia Butler…

19.title: Apply Doula Support in a Real Birth
19.description: Enroll in a doula apprenticeship program and volunteer to support a client during a birth, noting the strategies used to manage tension and keep the process smooth. Reflect in a journal after each session.

19.title: Write a Daily Transformation Journal
19.description: Commit to writing daily entries that explore how your creative or healing practices influence personal growth and social change. Use prompts like "What revolutionary idea did I express today?" or "How did my work support another's authenticity?"

19.title: Analyze Visionary Science‑Fiction Readings
19.description: Select a novel by Octavia Butler or another visionary author, read it actively, and summarize how the narrative challenges current power structures. Share your insights in a small discussion group or online forum.

19.title: Facilitate a Healing Workshop on Authenticity
19.description: Design a one‑hour workshop that creates a 'dressing room' for participants to try on authentic selves, using guided exercises, mirrors, and group sharing to foster self‑acceptance.

26.title: Map Your Emergent Strategy
26.description: Use the provided assessment tool to evaluate how much emergent strategy is currently present in your personal and work life. Identify at least three specific areas where emergent thinking is missing or weak.
26.sourceSentence: Towards the end is a brief assessment tool you can use to reflect on how much emergent strategy is showing up in your life and work.

26.title: Practice Emergent Tools
26.description: Select one emergent strategy practice or tool mentioned in the text and apply it to a real‑time project or routine. After implementation, document the experience and outcomes to build skill and confidence.
26.sourceSentence: Then I share some of the emergent strategy practices and tools I have worked with to create tangible differences in movement work.

26.title: Reflect on Cultural Conditioning
26.description: Write a short essay or journal entry exploring how Western socialization ('nature vs. nurture', 'anti-nurturing') has limited your use of emergent processes. Connect these insights to concrete steps you can take to practice emergent decision‑making.
26.sourceSentence: We learn to disrespect Indigenous and direct ties to land. We learn to be quiet, polite, indirect, and submissive, not to disturb the status quo.
